title: The Cosmic Neutrino Background Detection
bottleneck: Big Bang cosmology predicts a cosmic neutrino background of ~336 neutrinos per cubic centimeter, a pillar of the hot Big Bang as firm as the CMB — yet it has never been directly detected. Proposed tritium-capture experiments (PTOLEMY) face backgrounds and energy-resolution challenges that may be insurmountable with current technology. The capture cross-section on tritium is minuscule, requiring hundreds of grams of tritium and sub-eV energy resolution simultaneously.
why_it_blocks: Direct detection would confirm the universe's thermal history back to one second after the Bang; failure leaves a central prediction forever indirect.
current_state: PTOLEMY remains in R&D with no detection timeline; cosmological N_eff measurements are the only current handle. No funded experiment is close to the required sensitivity; the CNB may remain undetected for many decades.
